what: At each dot on the panel a chocolate strand hangs down. A strand is 3~11 balls (radius 12~24px, the upper half tapering by .85 each and the end a .88× droplet) joined and melted together with a goo filter (blur 4 · alpha 12 −4). Over 6~12 seconds it grows to 18~106px with cubic-bezier(.42,0,.12,1), then the end droplet falls (initial speed 100×period px/s, gravity 9.81), and over 5% of the period it rewinds quickly with (1−t)^5 and grows again. Thickness, length, period and initial phase differ for each strand on every open. It runs at 60fps only while the panel is near the screen (within 200px below)

options.[data-fx-part=point]: The point the line hangs from — the line stretches down from its center. The line color is the point’s text color (color, default --fx-drip → --kf-ink)
options.--fx-z: Canvas stacking order (css), default 10 — set it high if it flows over text

use:
…
— The canvas covers the panel that holds the parts, so include the empty space where the lines drip down in the panel
note: Dots usually attach to the bottom edge of a dark panel so they melt and drip from it. Safari finds the SVG filter heavy on canvas, so the consuming side may turn off the filter on .fx-goo-canvas (only the connected-ball shape remains)

from.where: shared.js drip panel (original data-drip-section — drip-canvas of the hero lower tier, product guide cards and feature cards)
